In Ladner Rural, Delta, the 55+ homes you can buy are South Pointe (strata). This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.

items.t: What the feed actually contains, in two clusters: (a) float homes on West River Road — six of the cards read are units at 3459, 3473 or 3871 West River Road, several of whose listing texts name the Canoe Pass float-home community and private boat slips; and (b) acreage and farm parcels inland — listings on 34B Avenue and a land-only parcel on 64 Street with Highway 17 frontage, per their listing texts. The acreage figures in those texts are feed composition only, not verified parcel facts.

Municipality and plan: City of Delta. The inland farm ground is planned under the Delta Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 8400 (2024) — a single consolidated plan with no lettered area-plan schedules — which designates farm land Agriculture (A), the designation whose stated purpose is to maintain agricultural lands.
Farm zoning: the A1 Agriculture zone of the Delta Zoning Bylaw is the zone intended for farming, breeding pets, kennels and related uses.
Nearby areas: Ladner Village and its sub-areas (Hawthorne, Holly, Delta Manor, Neilsen Grove) to the east, East Delta beyond them, and Tsawwassen to the south.

Where Ladner's verified 55+ housing actually is, for contrast: in the village, not the rural belt — Delta Green at 4686 51 Street in the village core and South Pointe, a gated bare land strata in Neilsen Grove, plus the subsidized village rentals. None sits in Ladner Rural.

Transit: TransLink route 601 runs via Ladner Exchange, Ladner Trunk Road, Highway 17A and Highway 99 to Bridgeport Station, and Ladner Exchange sits beside Delta Hospital. A bus route serving West River Road itself: Not verified — no TransLink timetable opened shows one.
Health: Delta Hospital, 5800 Mountain View Blvd, Delta, is Fraser Health's community hospital for Delta with 24/7 emergency care — in the village, on the urban side of the belt.

items.t: The strata age-bylaw rules, for the record — with no local 55+ strata to apply them to: Only 55+ age bylaws are legal in BC strata now (Strata Property Act, ss. 123.1 and 123.2; age bylaws below 55 invalid since Nov 24, 2022, under Bill 44); the bylaw restricts residency, not ownership; Strata Property Regulation 7.01 exempts legacy residents, live-in caregivers, and — expanded May 1, 2023 — a younger spouse or partner, children under 19 in the specified resident's care, and adult children cared for before 19; and residential rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022, while short-term restrictions remain allowed. A Ladner Rural farm buyer gets none of this machinery, because a farm purchase is freehold land, not a strata lot — and the one strata in the sub-area, Canoe Pass Village, has no verified age bylaw.

ALR housing caps are the rules that actually bind a 55+ farm buyer: Land in the ALR may generally have no more than one residence per parcel unless an additional residence qualifies; a principal residence built without an ALC application must have a total floor area of 500 m² or less, and a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence; local governments may further regulate or restrict residences in the ALR. ALR residences cannot be stratified.

The second-dwelling rule is the ageing-in-place rule on a farm: The ALC permits one additional residence without an ALC application where its conditions are met — detached, with a total floor area of 90 m² or less on parcels of 40 ha or smaller and 186 m² or less on parcels larger than 40 ha — and Delta's bylaws must also permit it. That is the legal route to a caregiver's or family member's dwelling on a Ladner Rural farm; anything larger needs an ALC application.

Delta's A1 zone states the same limits in the bylaw: one farm house per lot, maximum total floor area 500 m², on a farm home plate of at most 3,600 m² (5,000 m² where an additional farm house is also on the plate); one accessory farm dwelling unit per lot at the 90 m² / 186 m² limits on the same farm home plate; an additional farm house requires a Professional Agrologist's necessity report and written ALC approval; and subdivision in A1 is not permitted except with OCP compliance and Agricultural Land Commission Act approval where applicable, with a minimum lot size of 8 ha apart from the home site severance exception. A parcel's ALR status is checked on the ALC maps by PID or civic address, and the ALC states its online tools are for general reference only.
: The West River Road cards are float homes in a marina setting per their listing texts, with boat slips described as part of, or rented through, the complex.

Farm classification is a continuing obligation, not a one-time label: BC Assessment's minimum gross farm income requirements at farm gate prices are $2,500 if the farm operation is between 0.8 ha and 4 ha, $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area in excess of 4 ha if the operation is greater than 4 ha, and $10,000 if the operation is less than 0.8 ha. A downsizing buyer who stops producing can lose the classification and its tax treatment.

Water, drainage and flood are operating rules here, not background: the City of Delta operates and maintains 31 drainage pump stations and approximately 538 kilometres of drainage infrastructure, and over 63 kilometres of flood protection infrastructure — dikes, seawalls and foreshore protection; in the agricultural area the ditches and pump stations function in drainage mode in winter and in irrigation mode in summer, with control gate structures regulating water levels. Parcel-level flood construction levels: Not verified for any parcel.

items.t: The page title and the page feed describe two different markets. A 55+ buyer opening this page for a seniors acreage community finds neither: no age-restricted product in either cluster.

The ladner-farms page's feed spans Ladner Rural plus East Delta (and its research took in Westham Island), because that page's feed carried East Delta listings; this page's feed is labelled Ladner Rural only, so East Delta farm stock and Westham Island are not imported here.

Delta's 2024 OCP is a single consolidated plan with no area-plan schedules. Bylaw No. 8400 (2024) designates the belt Agriculture (A); any citation of a lettered Tsawwassen/Ladner area-plan schedule or a "Schedule D.1" for this land belongs to the superseded OCP and is wrong for current planning.

The ditches change jobs with the season. In Delta's agricultural area the same ditch and pump-station system drains the land in winter and irrigates crops in summer under City control gates — a retired farmer buying for quiet rural living is buying into a working water system, with ditch, drainage and irrigation positions to get from the City, not from a listing.

Ladner's newest 55+ ownership building is in the village, and it is recent. Delta Green at 4686 51 Street was built in 2021 — 24 strata units, plan EPS8064 — and its 2018 public hearing record shows the 55+ category was in the proposal from the start. The village, not the belt, is where Delta approves age-restricted strata.

faq.a: No — none was verified in any source. There is no age-restricted strata, park, co-op or life lease in the sub-area; the housing is freehold farm parcels and the all-ages Canoe Pass float homes on West River Road. Ladner's verified 55+ purchases (Delta Green, South Pointe) are in the village.
faq.q: Is there any 55+ home I can actually buy in Ladner Rural?

faq.a: No source states an age restriction for it. It is a 43-home floating-home strata community per the Floating Homes Association listing, in the Ladner Rural sub-area per listing data — a marina lifestyle community, not an age-restricted one.
faq.q: Is Canoe Pass Village a 55+ community?

faq.a: On ALR land, a principal residence built without an ALC application is capped at 500 m² total floor area, and a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence; Delta's A1 zone repeats the 500 m² farm house cap and the farm home plate maximum of 3,600 m². Confirm the parcel's ALR status on the ALC maps before designing anything.
faq.q: I'm 55+ and buying a farm to downsize onto. What limits the house I can build?

faq.a: The ALC permits one additional residence without an application where its size rules are met — 90 m² or less on parcels of 40 ha or smaller, 186 m² or less on larger parcels, detached — and Delta's bylaws must also permit it; Delta's A1 zone places that accessory farm dwelling unit on the same farm home plate as the farm house. There is no strata-style caregiver exemption here because there is no strata; the land rules are the whole answer.
faq.q: Can my adult child or a caregiver live in a second dwelling on the farm?

faq.a: Only within tight limits: in the A1 zone a new lot created by subdivision needs a minimum of 8 ha, Official Community Plan compliance and Agricultural Land Commission Act approval where applicable, with a home site severance exception under ALC policy.
faq.q: Can I subdivide a Ladner Rural farm parcel for family lots?

faq.a: Not automatically: BC Assessment requires a producing farm to keep meeting minimum gross farm income thresholds that scale with the operation's size ($2,500 at 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha above that; $10,000 under 0.8 ha). Plan the production, or lease the land to someone who produces, before assuming the classification survives.
faq.q: If I stop farming, do I keep farm-class taxes?

faq.a: Not confirmed from the sources checked: the listings describe float homes with boat slips in a strata-style marina community, but no official or strata source for the Canoe Pass community's tenure, moorage or legal structure was opened, and listing text does not establish what is owned, what moorage costs, or how lenders and insurers treat the home. Diligence the tenure documents before the lifestyle.

faq.a: Farm classification is a separate BC Assessment matter and is not affected by deferment.
